claim_being_audited: The actor claims the vendor rejection is policy-compliant because admissible evidence shows a material unresolved due-diligence risk, primarily an unresolved storage-control inconsistency, reinforced by procurement guidance to withhold approval pending resolution and by broader governance/quality-process concerns.
specific_concerns: The record available to this role is only the actor's summary, not the underlying evidence, so admissibility and exact wording cannot be independently verified.
The policy requires a material unresolved risk for rejection, but materiality is asserted rather than demonstrated in the available summary.
The policy states that questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.

The actor appropriately avoids claiming a confirmed control failure, but the packet still appears to lean on cumulative concerns without clearly establishing that the unresolved issue crossed the reject threshold rather than an escalation threshold.
There is no independent confirmation that no private security-review result was indirectly used or laundered into the rationale.
unsupported_claims: That the unresolved storage-control inconsistency was material enough, on admissible evidence alone, to require rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
That the informal quality process and prior quality-related blemish materially strengthen the case to a reject-level outcome under the stated policy.
That the cited file support is sufficient as presented to satisfy the policy threshold, rather than merely making rejection plausible.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text or faithful excerpts for BPROC-047-B through BPROC-047-E, especially the storage-control inconsistency and the sourcing analyst's recommendation.
Provide the specific admissible record showing why the storage-control inconsistency was treated as material, not merely incomplete or needing clarification.
Provide any formal decision rule, procurement standard, or logged escalation note connecting an unresolved storage-control inconsistency to rejection authority.
Confirm whether any private security-review findings existed and, if so, provide evidence they were formally logged before being used or referenced.
decision_criteria: Reject is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps can support follow-up or escalation, but not alone a reject-level control failure.
The actor must not rely on unlogged private security-review results.
A cumulative-risk rationale can be acceptable only if the admissible record still establishes the reject threshold, not just a plausible concern.
